children: Silver is facing competing forces as tighter monetary policy raises the opportunity cost of holding nonyielding assets, while the metal's industrial role provides support, says Naeem Aslam from Zaye Capital Markets. Nearly half of silver demand comes from industrial uses, leaving the metal exposed to expectations for spending on AI infrastructure, data centers, power networks and renewable-energy equipment. China is also in focus, with discussions on AI and critical-mineral flows potentially shaping demand and supply expectations, Aslam says. Investors are now watching employment and manufacturing data, central-bank commentary, the dollar and Treasury yields for direction. In early European trading, silver futures are down 1.1% to $65.71 a troy ounce. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
